items.title: Tech Earnings Are the Market’s Biggest Story This Week: Here’s Why Microsoft, Amazon, Intel, SanDisk, and Alphabet Will Drive the Stock Market’s Next Move
items.summary: This could be the most important week of 2026 for AI stocks. Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL), Intel (NASDAQ: INTC), and SanDisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) are preparing to report earnings, and the results could determine where the technology sector heads next. In this video, Eric Bleeker, CFA, Chief Investment Officer of 24/7 Wall St., previews the biggest earnings announcements and explains what investors should watch as concerns about artificial intelligence spending continue to pressure technology stocks. After sharp declines across AI infrastructure companies, Wall Street is increasingly questioning whether the hundreds of billions of dollars being invested in data centers will generate sufficient returns. Microsoft's Azure growth, Amazon Web Services' accelerating revenue, and Alphabet's expanding AI infrastructure investments will be especially important. Meanwhile, Intel, SanDisk, and SK Hynix could provide critical insight into demand for semiconductors, memory, and AI hardware. We'll break down earnings expectations, the most important numbers to watch, and why this week's results could either reignite enthusiasm for AI stocks or accelerate the selloff.

analysis.summary: Microsoft and Amazon are among a slate of tech giants reporting earnings this week, a focal point for market direction as investors gauge AI‑related growth.
analysis.catalyst: Upcoming Q2 2026 earnings releases for Microsoft (MSFT) and Amazon (AMZN)
analysis.horizon: 3-5 days, until the earnings press release and initial market reaction are digested
analysis.explanation: The market is zeroing in on this week’s earnings because AI spending is accelerating and both Microsoft and Amazon are key beneficiaries. Microsoft’s Azure AI revenue has been growing double‑digits, and Amazon’s AWS AI services are expanding their margin. A neutral sentiment reading suggests the news isn’t overly priced in yet, leaving upside potential if either beats expectations. Over the next few days the earnings numbers and guidance will drive the stock, while broader market sentiment remains supportive of tech. Holding the stock directly captures the upside without the complexity of options, and the short‑term horizon limits exposure to longer‑term valuation concerns.
rationale: AI‑related revenue streams are accelerating for both firms
Earnings week is a known market catalyst that often moves stocks 3‑5% on surprise
Neutral sentiment implies upside is not fully priced in
analysis.risk: If both companies miss revenue or guidance expectations, the stocks could drop sharply, eroding the short‑term gain.

The forward P/E of 14.6 is modestly above the sector average, suggesting room for upside if earnings confirm growth. With a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) and a PEG of 2.43, the market may be undervaluing the growth story, making a modest long position attractive. The trade is best expressed as a straight equity position to capture the earnings‑driven move, rather than options which add unnecessary complexity for a short‑term swing.
rationale: Earnings forecast shows strong top‑line and EPS growth
Current price reflects a modest premium, leaving upside potential
Technical pull‑back creates a better entry point before the catalyst
analysis.risk: If ADM misses earnings expectations or issues weaker guidance, the stock could fall further, eroding the short‑term upside.

analysis.summary: Pfizer’s forward P/E rose to about 11x despite lower earnings estimates, and the upcoming Q3 earnings on Nov 3 will test whether the higher multiple is justified.
analysis.catalyst: Pfizer Q3 earnings release on November 3, 2024
analysis.horizon: 3-5 days, until the Q3 earnings results are released and the forward multiple reaction is clear
analysis.explanation: Pfizer’s stock has climbed to $30, trading above the consensus $29 target, while its forward P/E jumped from 9 to 11 despite analysts cutting the next‑12‑month EPS estimate. This suggests investors are paying more for less earnings, a classic overvaluation signal. The key test will be the Q3 earnings on Nov 3; if revenue and EPS miss expectations, the multiple is likely to compress back toward 9x, pushing the price lower. With a neutral sentiment reading and a target price below current levels, a short position captures the downside risk. The trade is focused on the equity itself rather than a broader pharma ETF because the catalyst is company‑specific earnings data.
rationale: Higher forward P/E despite lower earnings forecasts signals overvaluation
Q3 earnings will confirm if growth in launched/acquired products can sustain the premium
Target price (~$29) is below current price, implying downside potential
analysis.risk: If Pfizer beats revenue and EPS expectations, the forward multiple could stay elevated and the stock may rally, eroding the short thesis.

items.title: Up 35%, How Long Can Coca-Cola Continue Crushing the S&P 500?
items.summary: Coca-Cola has had its best year since 1996.

analysis.summary: Coca‑Cola (KO) has outperformed the S&P 500 with a 35% YTD return, but its valuation (P/E 29) is far above rival PepsiCo’s (P/E 17) and its dividend yield is lower, raising questions about future demand for the stock.
analysis.catalyst: Recent comparative analysis showing PepsiCo’s improving fundamentals and cheaper valuation relative to Coca‑Cola
analysis.horizon: 3‑6 months, until the next earnings release (Q4 2026) clarifies whether KO can sustain its premium valuation
analysis.explanation: Coca‑Cola has delivered a strong 35% total return YTD, beating the S&P 500, but that performance is largely price‑driven and not backed by superior growth—its revenue outlook is only 4% for 2026, similar to PepsiCo’s 6% recent quarter growth. The market is rewarding KO at a 29x earnings multiple, while PepsiCo trades at just 17x, creating a sizable valuation gap. Moreover, KO’s dividend yield (2.2%) lags PepsiCo’s 4.2%, making the stock less attractive to income‑focused investors. Given the positive sentiment but the valuation head‑wind, a neutral stance lets us stay invested while we watch the upcoming earnings and any further guidance that could either justify the premium or trigger a pull‑back. If KO’s earnings beat and guidance improves, we could flip to long; if the gap widens, a short could be considered.
rationale: KO’s YTD outperformance is strong but not supported by superior growth
Large valuation premium vs. PepsiCo (29x vs 17x) could compress if earnings don’t accelerate
Lower dividend yield makes KO less appealing to income investors
analysis.risk: If Coca‑Cola’s earnings and guidance beat expectations, the premium valuation could be reinforced, causing the stock to keep rising and invalidating a neutral stance.
